scope: S1-S6 first-use and existing production call graph at current main; no broad historical report or cloud re-review.

findings.certainty: deterministic source call graph; no Apple/SDK/device runtime reproduction
findings.problem: A successful first signing-material publication does not promote the same live App session from unavailable/access=nil to signing. The current Settings flow then keeps pairing import and manual IPA preparation disabled until a later App lifecycle bootstrap.

trace.fact: initializeSigningNamespace persists configuration/namespace but intentionally publishes unavailable with signingMaterials and leaves coordinator/access nil.

refreshDeveloperMaterialsOwned receives the published lease, stores DeveloperMaterialObservation and returns; it does not resolve/activate the newly usable namespace or publish a fresh signing Status.
refreshDeveloperMaterials copies session.status after material publication. That status is still the prior unavailable/access=nil value.
The first-enrollment reconciliation and publication-finalization paths also return observations without reconnecting the App signing connection.
Manual IPA preparation requires owner.status.access == signing.
Settings entry only observes anisette registration; completion of refresh/reconcile/finalize invokes no bootstrap.

reachableScenario: Fresh valid installed app; initialize using real public enrollment input without caller namespace/device.
Configure the explicitly chosen anisette provider and successfully sign in.
Refresh signing materials successfully through the real account/Vault publication path.
Remain in the same foreground Settings session: status access is still nil, so pairing import/manual IPA preparation stay disabled.
findings.boundedImpact: A foreground/start bootstrap later resolves and activates the same valid published namespace; this is a missing immediate transition, not proof of a permanently disabled system or a failure of Apple material publication.

existingRecoveryEntry.fact: becameActive calls bootstrap; bootstrap resolves/activates the real existing connection.

findings.repairBoundary: After an acknowledged publication/reconciliation/finalization, reconnect through the existing full current-Bundle/Vault resolver and synchronize the Owner status. Never set signing access from the receipt alone or discard publication facts if later connection/status publication fails. A successful reconnect and failed/lost-ACK branch can be checked with owned fixtures before device validation.

facts: Tracked apple-public-enrollment.json now supplies schema1 and three public roots in each trust list, with namespaceID/device omitted.
initializeSigningNamespace reads those explicit inputs, verifies the actual Bundle, durably records one namespace intent and enters the sole Vault creation/resume path.
Owned test roots and injected trust/storage paths are DEBUG-only; production uses Bundle.main and default Keychain-backed owners.
developerServicesOwner creates the actual URLSession transport, Keychain session storage and AnisetteV3Provider from the explicitly configured endpoint. No service is selected by a fixture default.
Authentication executes the SRP/GSA handshake and explicit supported trusted-device secondary-auth path, then account.connect revalidates the remote account/team.

Material refresh reuses the persisted owned key, persists certificate-request intent before dispatch, verifies CSR-key/certificate/profile identity and commits through Vault.publish. Unknown issuance uses explicit reconciliation, not automatic duplicate CSR.
The confirmed first-publication transition gap above remains.
Existing PKCS12 import and possession/readback checks target a real App-accessible SecIdentity persistent reference; a JSON reference alone is not authority.

Pairing can be omitted during namespace initialization and material enrollment. Its later signing/no-active-transaction gate is an intentional prerequisite, not a namespace-to-pairing dependency loop.
The helper converts an existing user-supplied pairing record to local P12/public configuration; it neither manufactures a paired endpoint nor replaces initial signing roots.

productionChain.stage: S3/manual signed IPA and automatic currentApp archive
facts: The manual branch accepts an imported signed IPA and reaches the same full original verifier, fresh lease/identity validation, ControlledPackageSigner.resign, persisted candidate and mandatory verification. It does not accept an unsigned cloud IPA as trusted original input.

Automatic renewal uses withCurrentApplicationArchive on the real currently verified Bundle. It streams all inventory files, checks hashes before/after capture, validates the captured IPA, then enters ordinary prepareRenewalOwned.
No test-owned SDK fixture is substituted into either production branch.
Submission requires the persisted verified candidate and real configured pairing identity/endpoint, invokes authenticated Installer.upgrade and persists upload/upgrade intent before those writes.
beforeSubmission calls the existing App data handoff and commits its receipt before the first Upgrade frame.
Unknown submission recovers through the same authenticated Lookup/owned cleanup paths, without re-upload/resubmission.
Current-process installed-material observation and normal-load data observation remain separate from a transport receipt.
The existing App owner starts/binds the real BookStore/source/position owners, attempts the opt-in durably throttled use case on startup/foreground and schedules the registered processing identifier.
Info.plist contains com.yuedu.selfRenewal.processing in BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers and processing in UIBackgroundModes.

The same background runtime forwards cancellation and drains the actual worker before completion. Background-only launch without scene/owner binding can expire without starting renewal; the source explicitly preserves this limitation.

Automatic work still requires a valid current installed Bundle, stored account/service state, real pairing, due profile and no blocking unresolved transaction; lack of those prerequisites is not a stub.

remainingAcceptanceBoundaries: The first-publication reconnect gap can be fixed and behavior-tested with owned fixtures before device testing.
All actual SDK/crypto/signing/selected App tests must be judged from their final real outputs; this review does not infer any pending run result.
Real anisette provisioning, live GSA/2FA acceptance, same Personal Team/certificate/profile eligibility and service access still require actual authorization.
Existing pairing credentials, numeric endpoint reachability, same-device mTLS installation and system permission must be measured on the device.
Overwriting/restarting the actual signed app must prove the new profile expiry, current-process installed identity and normal-load user-data preservation.
iOS background scheduling is system granted; source wiring does not establish timing or unattended renewal.
reviewDoesNotReplace: all-source compatibility or complete S1-S6 acceptance
